In Lean, every concrete type other than the universes
and every type constructor other than dependent arrows
is an instance of a general family of type constructions known as inductive types.
It is remarkable that it is possible to construct a substantial edifice of mathematics
based on nothing more than the type universes, dependent arrow types, and inductive types;
everything else follows from those.
Intuitively, an inductive type is built up from a specified list of constructors.
For example, `List α` is the list of elements of type `α`, and is defined as follows:
```
inductive List (α : Type u) where
| nil
| cons (head : α) (tail : List α)
```
A list of elements of type `α` is either the empty list, `nil`,
or an element `head : α` followed by a list `tail : List α`.
See [Inductive types](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/inductive_types.html)
for more information.

  let modifiers : TSyntax ``Parser.Command.declModifiers := ⟨stx[0]⟩
  let decl     := stx[1]
  let declKind := decl.getKind
  if isDefLike decl then
    -- only case implementing incrementality currently
    elabMutualDef #[stx]
  else withoutCommandIncrementality true do
    -- use hash of declaration name, if any, as stable quot context; `elabMutualDef` has its own
    -- handling
    withInitQuotContext (getDeclName? stx |>.map hash) do
    let mut modifiers ← elabModifiers modifiers
    if (← getScope).isMeta && modifiers.computeKind == .regular then
      modifiers := { modifiers with computeKind := .meta }
    withExporting (isExporting := modifiers.isInferredPublic (← getEnv)) do

      else if declKind == ``Lean.Parser.Command.«inductive»
          || declKind == ``Lean.Parser.Command.«coinductive»
          || declKind == ``Lean.Parser.Command.classInductive
          || declKind == ``Lean.Parser.Command.«structure» then

h1e3f670807b63290.hover:
Makes names from other namespaces visible without writing the namespace prefix.

Names that are made available with `open` are visible within the current `section` or `namespace`
block. This makes referring to (type) definitions and theorems easier, but note that it can also
make [scoped instances], notations, and attributes from a different namespace available.

The `open` command can be used in a few different ways:

* `open Some.Namespace.Path1 Some.Namespace.Path2` makes all non-protected names in
  `Some.Namespace.Path1` and `Some.Namespace.Path2` available without the prefix, so that
  `Some.Namespace.Path1.x` and `Some.Namespace.Path2.y` can be referred to by writing only `x` and
  `y`.

* `open Some.Namespace.Path hiding def1 def2` opens all non-protected names in `Some.Namespace.Path`
  except `def1` and `def2`.

* `open Some.Namespace.Path (def1 def2)` only makes `Some.Namespace.Path.def1` and
  `Some.Namespace.Path.def2` available without the full prefix, so `Some.Namespace.Path.def3` would
  be unaffected.

  This works even if `def1` and `def2` are `protected`.

* `open Some.Namespace.Path renaming def1 → def1', def2 → def2'` same as `open Some.Namespace.Path
  (def1 def2)` but `def1`/`def2`'s names are changed to `def1'`/`def2'`.

  This works even if `def1` and `def2` are `protected`.

* `open scoped Some.Namespace.Path1 Some.Namespace.Path2` **only** opens [scoped instances],
  notations, and attributes from `Namespace1` and `Namespace2`; it does **not** make any other name
  available.

* `open <any of the open shapes above> in` makes the names `open`-ed visible only in the next
  command or expression.

[scoped instance]: https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/type_classes.html#scoped-instances
(Scoped instances in Theorem Proving in Lean)


## Examples

```lean
/-- SKI combinators https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SKI_combinator_calculus -/
namespace Combinator.Calculus
  def I (a : α) : α := a
  def K (a : α) : β → α := fun _ => a
  def S (x : α → β → γ) (y : α → β) (z : α) : γ := x z (y z)
end Combinator.Calculus

section
  -- open everything under `Combinator.Calculus`, *i.e.* `I`, `K` and `S`,
  -- until the section ends
  open Combinator.Calculus

  theorem SKx_eq_K : S K x = I := rfl
end

-- open everything under `Combinator.Calculus` only for the next command (the next `theorem`, here)
open Combinator.Calculus in
theorem SKx_eq_K' : S K x = I := rfl

section
  -- open only `S` and `K` under `Combinator.Calculus`
  open Combinator.Calculus (S K)

  theorem SKxy_eq_y : S K x y = y := rfl

  -- `I` is not in scope, we have to use its full path
  theorem SKxy_eq_Iy : S K x y = Combinator.Calculus.I y := rfl
end

section
  open Combinator.Calculus
    renaming
      I → identity,
      K → konstant

  #check identity
  #check konstant
end

section
  open Combinator.Calculus
    hiding S

  #check I
  #check K
end

section
  namespace Demo
    inductive MyType
    | val

    namespace N1
      scoped infix:68 " ≋ " => BEq.beq

      scoped instance : BEq MyType where
        beq _ _ := true

      def Alias := MyType
    end N1
  end Demo

  -- bring `≋` and the instance in scope, but not `Alias`
  open scoped Demo.N1

  #check Demo.MyType.val == Demo.MyType.val
  #check Demo.MyType.val ≋ Demo.MyType.val
  -- #check Alias -- unknown identifier 'Alias'
end
```

    (routes : C(unitInterval, P.BoundaryCurve)) (p l r : Plane) where
  homeomorph : range (closedRouteStripMap routes) ≃ₜ convexHull ℝ ({p, l, r} : Set Plane)

  convex_patches : ∀ (patch : Set Space), Convex ℝ patch →
    ∀ inclusion : C(patch, range (closedRouteStripMap routes)),
      (∀ x, ((inclusion x).val : Space) = (x : Space)) → Isometry (fun x => (homeomorph (inclusion x) : Plane))

      (∀ x, ((inclusion x).val : Space) = chart.map (x : Plane)) →
        Isometry (fun x => (homeomorph (inclusion x) : Plane))
  rigid_pieces : HasFiniteRigidPieces (convexHull ℝ ({p, l, r} : Set Plane))

structure CutVoronoiChart (P : ConvexPolyhedron) (a b : frontier P.body) extends P.FlatChart b where
  sources : Set Plane
  finite_sources : sources.Finite
  source_distance : ∀ p ∈ sources, dist p origin = P.surfaceDist a b
  route_count : sources.ncard = Nat.card (P.geodesicFiber a b)
  local_distance : ∀ x ∈ domain,
    (∀ p ∈ sources, P.surfaceDist a (map x) ≤ dist p x) ∧
      ∃ p ∈ sources, P.surfaceDist a (map x) = dist p x
  cut_diagram : ∀ x ∈ domain, map x ∈ P.multipleRouteLocus a ↔ x ∈ voronoiBoundary sources
  source_routes : ∀ p, p ∈ sources ↔ ∃ f ∈ P.geodesicFiber a b,
    ∃ start : unitInterval, start < 1 ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc start 1,
      AffineMap.lineMap p origin (t : ℝ) ∈ domain ∧
      map (AffineMap.lineMap p origin (t : ℝ)) = (f t : Space)
  route_stability : ∀ (p : Plane) (f : P.BoundaryCurve), f ∈ P.geodesicFiber a b →
    (∃ start : unitInterval, start < 1 ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc start 1,
      AffineMap.lineMap p origin (t : ℝ) ∈ domain ∧
      map (AffineMap.lineMap p origin (t : ℝ)) = (f t : Space)) →
    ∃ W : Set P.BoundaryCurve, IsOpen W ∧ f ∈ W ∧
      ∀ g ∈ W, g ∈ P.geodesicCurves → g 0 = a →
        ∀ x ∈ domain, map x = (g 1 : Space) → P.surfaceDist a (map x) = dist p x

theorem wedge_step_with_parameters
    (incoming outgoing : circularGapMidpoints fan.order.angles fan.order.first fan.order.last)
    (distinct : incoming ≠ outgoing) (ω : ℝ) (outer_lower : π / 2 ≤ ω)
    (budget : ω + (fan.triangles outgoing).model.sourceAngle ≤ 3 * π / 2) :
    let z := fan.order.chart.origin
    let d := P.surfaceDist a (T.vertexTarget u)
    let L := dist (u : Space) ((fan.order.neighbors outgoing).val : Space)
    let y := z + L • direction outgoing
    ∃ α β γ δ : ℝ,
      IsCircularGap fan.order.angles fan.order.first fan.order.last α β ∧
      IsCircularGap fan.order.angles fan.order.first fan.order.last γ δ ∧
      (incoming : ℝ) = (α + β) / 2 ∧ (outgoing : ℝ) = (γ + δ) / 2 ∧
      ∃ D Θ : ℝ, 0 < D ∧ 0 < Θ ∧ Θ < π ∧
        D = P.surfaceDist a (T.vertexTarget (fan.order.neighbors outgoing).val) ∧
        π - Θ = angle (fan.triangles outgoing).model.first
          (fan.triangles outgoing).model.right (fan.triangles outgoing).model.left ∧
        let W := {x | x - z ∈ polarRegion d ω α β}
        let V := {x | x - z ∈ polarRegion d ω δ (γ + 2 * π)}
        let W' := {x | x - y ∈ polarRegion D (ω + (fan.triangles outgoing).model.sourceAngle)
          (Θ + (γ + δ) / 2) (2 * π - Θ + (γ + δ) / 2)}
        W ⊆ V ∧ Disjoint V (interior (gapKite z d L γ δ)) ∧ W' = V ∪ gapKite z d L γ δ

    if getMainVersoModuleDocs (← getEnv) |>.isEmpty then
      let doc := String.Pos.Raw.extract val 0 (val.rawEndPos.unoffsetBy ⟨2⟩)

    let docSyntax := args.getD 0 .missing
    if docSyntax.getKind == `Lean.Doc.Syntax.parseFailure then

    else

        addVersoModDocString range ⟨docSyntax⟩
